samples.summary: Single-cell paste exemption assumes the written cell is the merge anchor; an HTML paste whose grid bounding box is offset from the target writes into a covered cell of a preserved merge
samples.evidence: `const overwrittenMerges = isSameRef(destRange[0], destRange[1]) ? [] : ...` (line 2285) skips the merge check entirely for a 1x1 paste range, justified by the comment "it writes through the anchor above". That justification holds only when the single grid cell *is* `target`. For the HTML branch, `html2grid` skips empty, unstyled ``s (`packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/grids.ts:179 if (!text && !el.style.cssText) continue;`) while still advancing the column index, so pasting `x` at A1 yields a grid of only `{B1: x}`. `pasteRange = this.gridRange(grid)` is then `B1:B1`, `isSameRef` is true, the merge check is skipped, and `setGrid` (which writes raw srefs, sheet.ts:1002-1004 → store.setGrid, no anchor normalization) stores 'x' into B1 — a cell covered by the surviving A1:B1 merge. That breaks the covered-cells-hold-no-content invariant the rest of this change relies on: the value is invisible, `getCell(B1)` returns the anchor's value while the store holds another, and the content reappears on unmerge. The exemption should compare the single cell to `target` (or normalize the grid through anchors) rather than only checking that the range is collapsed.

samples.summary: Internal paste of an empty copy buffer drops destination merged blocks even though no content is written
samples.evidence: For the internal branch `pasteRange` is set unconditionally from the translated `sourceRange` (lines 2236-2242) and is never checked against `grid.size`. Copying a range that contains no cells gives `grid.size === 0` and `grid2string(grid) === ''` (grids.ts:18-43 produces an empty table), so `paste({ text: '' })` matches `text === this.copyBuffer.text` and takes the internal branch. `overwrittenMerges` is then computed over the whole translated rectangle and every merge fully inside it is deleted at lines 2329-2339 while `setGrid` writes nothing — the user's merged block is silently destroyed by a paste that pastes nothing. Before this change an empty grid was effectively a no-op (`selectPastedRange` returned early).

samples.summary: Merges re-created by paste bypass the validation `canMergeSelection` enforces (frozen-pane crossing, sheet bounds)
samples.evidence: `for (const merge of pastedMerges) { await this.store.setMerge(...) }` (lines 2340-2348) creates merged blocks with no validation. `canMergeSelection()` (lines 4436-4452) refuses a merge that crosses `frozenRows`/`frozenCols`, and `pasteRange`/`pastedMerges` are computed by pure arithmetic (`target.r + (sourceRange[1].r - sourceRange[0].r)`, line 2239) with no clamping to `this.dimensionRange`. So copying a merged block and pasting it so that it straddles the frozen row/column boundary, or past the last row/column, produces merge state the merge UI itself considers illegal — the frozen panes are rendered separately, so a straddling block cannot be drawn consistently. `moveRangeTo` has the same gap, so this is a pre-existing hole the new paste path widens.

samples.summary: paste calls clearCellsUnderMerge without the `keep` predicate moveRangeTo passes, so cells the same paste just wrote can be deleted
samples.evidence: `moveRangeTo` passes `(sref) => movedGrid.has(sref)` (line 2571) so freshly written destination cells survive; the paste call at 2343-2347 passes no `keep`. It relies on the copied grid being sparse under merged blocks, which holds only while the covered-cells-hold-no-content invariant holds. If a covered source cell does carry content (state arriving from a collaborative store, or a merge whose covered cells were never cleared — note `mergeSelection` at 4485-4497 does not clear spill ghosts), `fetchGrid` captures it, `setGrid` writes it at the destination, and `clearCellsUnderMerge` then deletes it in the same batch: silent loss of a value the user just pasted.

samples.summary: Cut-paste mixes a stale merge snapshot with live merge state
samples.evidence: `pastedMerges` comes from `this.copyBuffer.merges`, captured at copy/cut time (lines 2153/2173), while `cutMerges` is recomputed from live state (`this.getMergesIntersecting(cutSourceRange)`, line 2274). If the merge layout changes between cut and paste (the user or a collaborator merges/unmerges inside the cut source), the two disagree: the split check at 2229 only inspects the stale snapshot, so a merge created after the cut and only partially inside the cut source is neither dropped nor refused, yet the source-deletion loop at 2361-2371 deletes its anchor's content, leaving an empty merged block behind. Conversely a merge unmerged after the copy is still re-created at the destination by `pastedMerges`.

samples.summary: The "refused paste keeps the cut buffer" behavior the diff adds does not hold through the view
samples.evidence: The diff deliberately moves `if (isCut) this.copyBuffer = undefined;` after the refusal checks (sheet.ts:2293-2295) "so a refused paste leaves the buffer intact", and merge.test.ts asserts `isCutMode() === true` after a refusal. But the view calls `this.sheet!.clearCopyBuffer()` immediately after every `paste()` (worksheet.ts:4899-4900), so in the real UI a refused cut-paste still discards the buffer and the user cannot retry the cut. The tested guarantee is model-only.

samples.summary: Pasted merge shares the same MergeSpan object as the source merge
samples.evidence: `this.merges.set(toSref(merge.anchor), merge.span)` (line 2342) stores the `span` object taken from `copyBuffer.merges`, which itself is the object held in `this.merges` for the source block (getMergesIntersecting returns `span` by reference, line 915). After a copy-paste two anchors share one span object, and pasting repeatedly shares it further; any in-place mutation of a span would corrupt every aliased block. Cloning the span would remove the hazard.

samples.summary: Paste unmerges destination blocks whose content it never replaces, leaving stale content in an inconsistent layout
samples.evidence: For an internal paste the drop set is computed over the whole translated rectangle (`getMergesIntersecting(destRange)`, line 2287) while `setGrid` only writes the sparse copied grid. A merge sitting in a blank part of the copied rectangle is therefore deleted while its content is left untouched — merge.test.ts:229-252 encodes exactly this (B3:C3 dropped, '20' still in B3). The destination ends up half-updated: layout removed, old values retained.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. sheet.ts:2285 exempts any collapsed paste bounding box from the merge-overwrite check, justified by the comment that the write goes "through the anchor" — but only `target` is anchor-normalized (sheet.ts:2194), not the grid keys. html2grid (grids.ts:179) skips empty, unstyled cells while still advancing `ci` and writes at `destRef.c + ci` (grids.ts:229), so an HTML paste like `x` at anchor A1 yields a grid whose sole key is B1; gridRange (sheet.ts:2265) makes pasteRange B1:B1, isSameRef is true, the intersecting A1:B1 merge is neither refused nor dropped, and setGrid (sheet.ts:1002-1004 → memory.ts:137-143) stores the value at the raw sref B1 with no anchor normalization. clearCellsUnderMerge runs only for pastedMerges (sheet.ts:2340-2348), which is empty on the HTML branch, so the covered cell retains hidden content that getCell masks (sheet.ts:988-989) and that reappears on unmerge. The plain-TSV branch (grids.ts:113-126) cannot go offset, so no other guard covers this path. Real, in-lane data-integrity/invariant defect.
